title: Land an agent's work from its pushed branch
prompt:
Make the integrator judge and land what an agent published, not what happens to be on the integrator's host. Read docs/storage.md (branches, the pusher, landing) and, in the code, `judge()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/push.rs and crates/spawn-cli/src/sources.rs first.

The integrator looks for `refs/heads/<agent>` in its own mirror of the mission's source and, when the agent's workspace directory exists under its root, commits that workspace first. So work done on another host never lands (the integrator's mirror has no such branch), and on the Bridge's own host a file the agent wrote after its last checkpoint, never pushed, lands with the task. Required behaviour:

1. The candidate is the source's `refs/heads/spawn/<agent>`, the branch the pusher publishes. Before judging, the integrator fetches it from the mission's source into a ref of its own in its mirror. Not `refs/heads/<agent>`: on the Bridge's host that branch belongs to the Bridge, and the integrator must never move it.
2. The integrator never commits a mounted workspace. It works the same when the agent's workspace, its local branch and the host that ran it do not exist on the integrator's host.
3. Stale pushes do not land. The integrator reads the commit of the agent's latest `artifact.committed` event (the Bridge's latest checkpoint or merge of main). The pushed head must be that commit or a descendant of it. Otherwise the push lags the checkpoint. That includes a checkpoint commit the fetched branch does not contain, and a source with no `spawn/<agent>` while the agent has a checkpoint. In that case the verdict is `stale`: the gate does not run, the task goes back to `reported` (or `accepted` under review), no rejection is counted and nothing is sent to the worker, and a later pass judges again once the pusher has caught up. An agent with no checkpoint and no pushed branch is rejected as "the worker has no branch to land".
4. Everything else the integrator does to a candidate is unchanged: a branch head carrying a `Spawn-Large` trailer lands as a commit of the same tree without it, a branch behind a moved main lands as the merge by main's merge rules, conflict marker blocks in the files the branch changes are gated `conflict`, the landing is a compare-and-swap push of the source's main. A pending merge of main lives with the workspace directory on the Bridge's host; it still blocks judging when that directory is on the integrator's host, and its markers, once checkpointed and pushed, are caught by the marker check wherever the integrator runs.

State the stale rule in docs/storage.md (landing) and in the integrator's module comment, and update the table of where state lives. Add unit tests for the rule (equal, descendant, behind, diverged, no pushed branch).

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/004.sh (read it). Real Bridges on separate workspace roots ("hosts") do the work with a fake engine, the pusher publishes `spawn/<agent>` to a local source, and a recording gate (SPAWN_GATE) accepts every candidate. (1) Agent X works on a host whose root is then deleted. An integrator on a fresh root lands the task: main gets X's file and the pushed branch's tree. (2) Agent Y checkpoints C1 then C2, and the source's spawn/Y is moved back to C1. On a fresh root and on Y's own host alike: main does not move, the task stays `reported` with no revision counted, and the host's own branch of Y stays at C2. (3) spawn/Y returns to C2 while Y is mounted on its host with a file written after C2. The integrator on that host lands exactly C2's tree, without that file. The scenario exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness or infrastructure failure.

Rules: never edit rsi/, scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/ or scripts/e2e.sh (the gate rejects any change there). The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]), and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. All existing checks must still pass: clippy, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios and the web build.
